text:
Maya: Hey — quick Q. Trying to call the Redwood JS SDK from inside a React Native app via a WebView. Calls to https://api.redwood.com keep failing with CORS preflight 403 and the Authorization header looks stripped. We mint short-lived tokens from our backend (5m) and rotate them. Anyone run into this and have a practical workaround?

Sam: React Native WebView runs in a weird browser context. Two common issues: (1) backend not allowing Authorization on preflight (OPTIONS) — make sure Access-Control-Allow-Headers includes Authorization, Content-Type; (2) some RN fetch/XHR polyfills drop or don't forward headers. If you control backend, also add Access-Control-Expose-Headers for any headers you inspect.

Jordan: For streaming specifically, WebView often buffers chunked responses / fetch streams, so SSE or fetch ReadableStream won't behave like a normal browser. If your app relies on streaming tokens or chunked tokens, consider a websocket fallback or move streaming into a native module (iOS/Android) that talks to the runtime libs directly.

Oliver: If you want minimal changes: add a tiny server-side proxy that attaches Authorization on the server and forwards requests to Redwood. This avoids CORS entirely and keeps long-lived keys only on your backend. Example proxy call from RN WebView: `fetch('/api/redwood-proxy', {method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({path: '/v1/generate', input})})` — proxy uses server-side key to call Redwood.

Maya: That proxy is probably simplest for now. Any tips for safe token rotation though? We're worried about leaking any usable token from the WebView.

Sam: Best practice: never embed primary API keys in the mobile client. Use your backend to mint ephemeral tokens (1–10m). Client asks your backend for a short token when it needs it. For stealth refresh, have the native layer refresh tokens out-of-band and postMessage to the WebView. If the WebView must perform direct calls, keep token lifetime short and require revalidation.

Jordan: Also watch out for OPTIONS requiring auth — browsers will preflight before sending Authorization. Make sure your OPTIONS handler returns 200 without requiring Authorization, and includes: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <your-origin>`, `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET,POST,OPTIONS`, `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization,Content-Type`. If you see OPTIONS returning 401, that's exactly why header gets "stripped" (preflight failed).

Sam: For React Native (not WebView) consider shipping small native wrappers (Swift/Kotlin) that call Redwood over TLS from native socket — no CORS. We have an internal example of an iOS wrapper that handles streaming via URLSession and exposes a lightweight bridge.

DevBot: deploy-bot: FYI — deployed staging fix for /proxy CORS headers (Added Allow-Headers and exposed headers) at 2025-11-14T09:12Z :rocket:

Maya: Awesome — I'll try the proxy + short-lived tokens + a native refresh flow. If I hit streaming issues we'll look at a simple native wrapper. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
